In the chat list top bar you find two filter buttons next to the star: the red flag shows only chats that contain to-do messages, the green check only chats with processed messages. Filters can be combined with each other and with search.

Swipe left on a chat or message to delete it (a confirmation dialog appears first). Swipe right on a chat to toggle its important status. Swipe right on a message inside a chat to cycle through: red flag (to-do), green check (processed) and no marking.

The text signature is appended to every outgoing email. The key signature is only appended to encrypted emails: it contains your OpenPGP public key (or a link to it) so the recipient can add you to their keyring and reply encrypted.

Mailchat is a dialog-based email client that shows your emails as messenger-style chats. Features: multiple IMAP accounts, group chats, favorites, important markers, account colors, auto sync, signature, search, dark mode, voice messages, end-to-end encryption (OpenPGP), and AI (on-device or cloud: spam detection, summaries, reply suggestions), and more.

Use the AI Summarize action in the chat (long-press a message, or select several messages) to summarize emails to 5 lines. It also runs spam classification and custom tag assignment, identical to the overview. The original email remains available in the detail view. The summary is written in your selected language.

Two AI providers are available:

ON-DEVICE (Gemma via Google LiteRT): The model runs directly on your phone. No email content ever leaves the device and no internet is needed after the one-time model download (0.5–3 GB). Limitations: the small models (2–4B parameters) are slower, less accurate and consume more battery than cloud models.

OPENAI API (OpenAI-compatible): You configure your own endpoint, API key and model. This usually gives better quality and faster answers, but your email content is sent to that external server.

All AI features (spam/phishing classification, custom tags, summaries, reply suggestions, real name extraction, appointment extraction, assistant) work with both providers — only the engine behind them changes.

Available AI features: spam/phishing classification, custom tag detection, message summaries, reply suggestions (formal/informal), real name extraction, appointment extraction and the assistant (chat with your data).

On-Device: fully local and private, but limited by the small model size (2–4B) — lower accuracy, slower, higher battery use.

OpenAI API: better quality, but email content is sent to your configured server.

Not yet available: streaming/real-time answers, translation, and rewriting/editing of existing text. On-device models cannot match cloud-model quality for complex tasks.

The purple "AI" tag appears on individual emails in the chat view when an AI summary has been generated. In the chat list overview, the highest spam category tag (Phishing, Unwanted, Newsletter) is shown instead.
The subject field above the compose bar lets you pick a subject from the conversation or type your own. Use the dropdown arrow to see all subjects from this chat.
Tap the star icon in the chat list top bar to show only your favorite and important chats. The star turns yellow when the filter is active. Tap again to show all chats.
The sender account selected in Settings (E-Mail → Sender account) sends all emails over its own SMTP server. Without a selection, each chat sends over its own account.
Use "Contact Developer" in Settings to open a chat with the developer directly in the app. The subject is pre-filled with "Help Request for MailChat".

If the sender of a chat is one of your known contacts, the chat header shows the contact photo and the contact name instead of the email address. If the contact is unknown, the circle uses the color of the account the chat belongs to.

Use "AI reply" (in the "+" menu next to the subject or in the message menu via long press) to write a reply. You choose between a formal (you) or a personal (you) tone. The AI creates a fitting subject and uses any text already in the reply field as a starting point.
In landscape mode and on tablets the screen is split: the chat list is shown on the left and the selected chat on the right. In portrait mode on a phone the usual single-screen navigation is used.

Emails with embedded images (e.g. from Deutsche Post) show the text in the chat bubble. Open the email (tap the bubble) and use the "Load images" button to display the embedded images on the detail page.

Incoming emails are automatically analyzed by AI for spam, phishing, and unwanted ads. A combination of heuristic rules (domain mismatch, urgency phrases, suspicious links) and AI classification determines the category. The result is shown as a colored tag on the email in the chat.

When filtering by "Phishing" in the filter sheet, the average phishing probability percentage is displayed. The probability is calculated from heuristic indicators such as domain mismatches, lookalike domains, urgency language, and suspicious URLs.

The purple "AI" tag appears on individual emails in the chat view when an AI summary has been generated. In the chat list overview, the highest spam category tag (Phishing, Unwanted, Newsletter) is shown instead.

Define your own tags (name + short description). The AI reads each incoming email and automatically assigns the matching tag — for example "Invoice", "Package" or "Private". You can also set a tag manually on a chat. Tags are shown as a colored label in the chat list and in the conversation, and you can filter the chat list by tag.

For emails classified as phishing or unwanted ads, images are blocked by default in the detail view to protect against tracking pixels and malicious content. Newsletter images are still loaded. You can manually enable image loading if needed.

MailChat uses standard OpenPGP (RFC 4880) encryption via BouncyCastle. Setup: 1) Generate your OpenPGP key in Settings (select your account). 2) When you send, MailChat automatically looks up the recipient\'s public key by email address on keys.openpgp.org (you can turn this off in Settings → Encryption). If it isn\'t published, exchange keys via QR code (show/scan), NFC (hold phones together), or email (send/paste the MAILCHAT_OG string). You can also publish your own public key to keys.openpgp.org (Settings → Encryption) so others can find it by your email address. 3) Once a key is available, a short fingerprint appears. Call the recipient and compare: tell them yours, ask for theirs. Tapping (i) copies the full fingerprint to clipboard. Security note: The short fingerprint (first 4 chars) is a human-friendly comparison aid, not a cryptographic mechanism — the real security comes from comparing the full fingerprint. Once a key is available, the message body and attachments are encrypted end-to-end. Contacts with an OpenPGP key show a green lock on their photo, contacts with the legacy MailChat key show a blue lock. The private key never leaves your device, and its passphrase is stored encrypted in the Android Keystore. To move your key to another device, export the private key (Settings → Encryption) and choose a passphrase for the exported file — you will need the same passphrase when importing it (leave it empty to export without protection). Limitations: automatic key lookup only works if the recipient has published their key on keys.openpgp.org; restoring your identity from a backup only works on the same device (the Keystore key is device-specific).

Long-press a message or chat to enter selection mode. Use the edit menu (top right) for batch actions: select all, invert, select by direction, mark as processed, set spam category, AI summarize, and more. Swipe right-to-left to deselect, left-to-right to select. The edit menu stays open until you exit selection mode.

Tap the filter icon (top right) to open the filter dropdown. Toggle filters for favorites, unread, processed, todo, hidden, phishing, unwanted, newsletter, and custom tags. The badge shows the total number of active filters including custom tags.
The "Unread" filter shows only chats that have unread messages. Enable it from the filter dropdown menu.
In the email detail view, use two fingers to pinch and zoom in/out on the content. This is useful for reading small text or examining images closely.

Select one or more chats, then use Edit → AI Summarize to generate summaries, categorize spam, and assign custom tags to all messages in the selected chats. Note: This takes approx. 30 seconds per email and may drain the battery.
Export all your data (accounts, chats, messages, settings) to a password-protected file. Import a backup to restore on a new device. The backup includes all local data but not server-side emails.

Choose who to reply to in a group chat. Your own address is hidden. Select "Send to all" to reply to everyone, or pick a specific person.\n\nAuto-reply \"Where are you?\" (1:1 chats only): when enabled, the app automatically replies to this contact with your current location when they ask \"Where are you?\" (recognized: \"wo bist du\", \"wo bist ihr\", \"wo seid ihr\", \"where are you\"). Notes and limitations: only incoming emails are checked; the location permission must be granted; the last known position is used, and if none is available a fresh GPS/network fix is requested (up to ~20 s, otherwise the reply is skipped and logged); the reply is sent only once per message; if the weather option is enabled, your location is sent to open-meteo.com to fetch the forecast for the next 4 hours.

Ask questions about your emails in natural language. The AI analyzes your local message data and provides answers, summaries, and insights. No data leaves your device unless AI is enabled. Note: The AI can only consider emails that fit within the configured context size (Settings → AI → Context Size, default 100,000 tokens). With small local models or low context sizes, not all emails may be included in the analysis. Increase the context size for more comprehensive results.
Manage your IMAP/SMTP email accounts. Add, edit, or remove accounts. Each account syncs incoming emails and can be used for sending.
Configure IMAP (receive) and SMTP (send) settings for this account. Host, port, encryption, and credentials. Test the connection before saving.
